title: brazil government extend gasoline subsidy until september 9 sources say 2026 08 25
text:
BRASILIA, Aug 25 (Reuters) - Brazil's government will extend a gasoline ​subsidy worth 0.44 reais ($0.0855) per liter until September ‌9, two sources close to the matter told Reuters on Tuesday.
The subsidy, which is paid to gasoline producers and importers and was created after the ​start of the U.S.-Iran conflict in the Middle ​East to curb the impact of rising global oil prices ⁠on domestic consumers, was set to end on Wednesday.
President ​Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's administration had last extended the subsidy ​on July 26 for another 30 days.
The government could not extend the benefit for another month this time since the presidential decree allowing ​its creation expires on September 9, and congressional approval remains ​pending.
Local newspaper Valor Economico first reported the government's plan earlier on Tuesday, ‌citing ⁠a source at the finance ministry. The ministry declined to comment.
In June, the government had decided to eliminate part of a diesel subsidy when oil prices retreated as tensions in ​the Middle East ​eased, but ⁠the external relief proved temporary amid a still-ongoing conflict.
The subsidies, among other measures aimed at ​the fuel sector, are part of a broad ​relief ⁠plan established by Lula since the start of the war in Iran. The leftist leader is seeking another four-year term in ⁠October's ​presidential election.
($1 = 5.1469 reais)
